executive_assessment.text: Selected Cabo Delgado sites, Nampula cyclone impacts and separately identified displacement drivers add local detail without merging weather and conflict causes.
Nankumi, Naminawe and Metula planning identifies equitable land/resource governance needs. Evaluation and government reports add capacity evidence, with implementation and causal limits retained.

geographic_notes.text: UNDP's selected Chiúre–Mecúfi–Pemba sample reports Cyclone Kenneth impacts alongside weak housing/sanitation and displacement-related vulnerability.

Source dated 2025-09-29 reports: UNDP's review cites earlier analysis that conflict-driven flight from homes and fields coincided with erratic-rainfall crop losses; displaced fishers also shifted to unfamiliar subsistence farming.

Source dated 2026-02-09 reports: In 2025, conflict drove major displacement from Memba District, Nampula: over 112,000 people fled, 65% children. Separately, about 15% of IDPs were in Sofala, mainly after climate shocks.

Source dated 2026-02-09 reports: Dikeledi and Jude affected over 1.3 million people in Q1 2025, mostly in Nampula, damaged 131 health facilities and 3,128 classrooms, and disrupted learning for 365,000-plus students.

Source dated 2026-02-09 reports: UNICEF deployed 3,924 mobile teams across 1,556 communities and resettlement sites; integrated brigades served hard-to-reach conflict- or climate-shock-affected areas in five named provinces.

Source dated 2025-11-21 reports: Evaluation finds humanitarian access in insecure northern districts constrained by conflict and instability; activity and staff training were interrupted in Cabo Delgado, while mobile brigades and boat clinics adapted delivery.

Source dated 2025-11-21 reports: Local consultative councils selected 86 climate-adaptive infrastructure projects; the evaluation also reports municipal upkeep of drainage machinery and Chókwè dike maintenance by local authorities.

Source dated 2026-08-26 reports: Cabo Delgado's conflict, displacement, climate exposure and resource pressure overlap in Nankumi (Ancuabe), Naminawe (Metuge) and Metula (Pemba); site selection noted host–IDP tension risk.

Source dated 2026-08-26 reports: Community-approved plans propose fairer land access, dialogue with government, reforestation, resilient agriculture and small dams, with community-led implementation intended.

Source dated not stated reports: Normal-to-above-normal northern and above-normal central/southern rains caused floods, road disruption and over 100,000 hectares inundated; Massingir Dam reduced impacts in Chókwè, Guijá, Chibuto and Xai-Xai.

Source dated 2026-08-13 reports: INGD reports eight anticipatory-action activations across six basins and for a cyclone (Dec 2025–Mar 2026), evacuating 7,214 people and warning about 1.5 million up to five days ahead; volunteers helped first when formal capacity was exceeded.

known_gaps.text: Climate projections: The verified NDC projection uses seven GCMs and specifies horizons but does not identify the emissions scenario associated with the cited 1.5-3.0°C mid-century range. Newer, district- or basin-resolved projections for heat, rainfall extremes, drought, sea-level rise and cyclone-related hazards should be independently assembled.

Geographic representation: The strongest direct climate-security evidence is from Mecufi. There is no comparable verified causal evidence in this packet for much of southern Mozambique, major cities, most of Zambézia/Nampula, major river basins or many conflict-affected northern localities.

Population differentiation: The NAP explicitly identifies vulnerable demographic groups but also acknowledges limited sex-disaggregated data. Disability, age, gender, return status, livelihood and urban-informal-settlement differences need more systematic measurement.

Causal uncertainty: Qualitative evidence supports several plausible climate -> livelihood/food/land -> FCV pathways, but no retained study establishes a national causal effect of climate shocks on violence, insurgent recruitment or communal conflict.

FCV-to-climate evidence: Evidence that conflict undermines adaptation is credible but mostly indirect or local - displacement, service overload, damaged institutions and natural-resource pressure. Comparative measurement of adaptation/recovery performance between conflict-affected and more stable districts is lacking.

Evaluation: Independent evaluation is available for the 2019 Idai humanitarian response and an older climate-mainstreaming programme, but current programmes - including 2024/25 anticipatory action and recent cyclone/flood responses - lack equivalent independent outcome evidence in the verified source set.

Unintended effects: Evidence is particularly thin on whether resettlement, land allocation, adaptation infrastructure, cash programmes, early-warning systems or ecosystem interventions inadvertently redistribute risk or generate grievances.

Access and verification: The World Bank CCDR full PDF exceeded the browsing crawler's size limit, and the WFP IAHE linked full report was not directly retrievable. Claims from both were therefore limited to their verified official publication pages. No unverified PDF-page claims from those documents have been retained.

*None are wholly absent, but four are only partially covered: coping-capacity, adaptive-capacity, direct-climate-fcv and resilience-peace-capacity. Response-performance is also partial because independent evaluations are dated or event-specific.

No inspected source establishes a causal effect of climate hazards on armed conflict or violence; the strongest direct links concern displacement, crop/food insecurity, resource access and potential host–IDP tensions.
UNDP Cabo Delgado fieldwork was conducted in 2023 in Chiúre, Mecúfi and Pemba, with some Metuge interviews; it is not representative of all districts or current 2026 conditions.
The OCHA 2026 humanitarian overview endpoint returned HTTP 403, and the FAO Open Knowledge page returned HTTP 403; neither was used for claims.
Recent government summaries document flooding and anticipatory response, but provide limited population-group disaggregation and no district-level counterfactual evaluation.
The 2026 community spatial plans in Ancuabe, Metuge and Pemba are proposed resilience and resource-governance measures; their implementation and effects on tensions remain unevaluated.

Main verified the original UNICEF mobile-team wording and UN community-plan release. Planned community actions and security-constrained general services are not promoted to evaluated adaptation/peace outcomes.
Cabo Delgado sample evidence is historical and site-selected; cyclone damage, northern conflict displacement and Sofala climate displacement are kept separate.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
